title: Experiment DSL + Runtime for Progressive Model Rollouts and Safety Attenuators
creator: Asha Kapoor
description:
Problem: teams need a reusable, auditable way to declare and run A/B/canary experiments for model variants that enforces conservative exposure, real-time statistical checks, shadow traffic wiring, and automatic remediation. Current ad-hoc scripts and infra tie experiments to one-off pipelines, creating risk (silent regressions, costly rollouts, manual rollbacks).

Proposal: ship an Experiment DSL (declarative YAML) plus a lightweight runtime service (Experiment Runner) that executes policies against live traffic. Core capabilities: declarative experiment spec, exposure controller with percentile-based throttles and cohort assignment, sequential/multi-metric statistical tests (alpha spending, early stopping), shadow routing mode, deterministic auto-rollback policies, and audit logs for compliance. Specs map directly to Redwood Console templates and API endpoints for self-serve experiments.

Scope: MVP covers text generation model A/B and canary scenarios (single primary vs variant), supports up to 3 cohorts, integrates with Smart Routing to pin traffic by region/plan, emits per-experiment telemetry to Console dashboards, and exposes APIs for start/stop/inspect. Does not include multi-armed bandit allocation or fully Bayesian posterior-ratio decisioning in MVP (limited to sequential frequentist checks with configurable error budgets).
acceptance_criteria: Teams can declare an experiment in YAML and start it via API/Console
Experiment Runner enforces configured exposure caps and cohort allocation deterministically
Sequential metric checks run every 5 minutes and can trigger automatic rollback when thresholds are crossed
Shadow mode can mirror 100% of selected traffic to a variant without user-visible exposure
All experiment decisions (start, pause, rollback) are recorded with operator and rationale in audit logs
Console shows per-experiment latency/cost/quality deltas and a statistical summary with p-values and confidence intervals

Prototype Experiment Runner service (Eng) with exposure controller and cohort allocator
Implement sequential statistical checks library (Research/Stats) and integrate into Runner
Console: experiment creation UI + template gallery (Design + Frontend)
Backend: APIs for start/stop/inspect + role-based access checks (Eng + Security)
Integrate shadow routing with Smart Routing and telemetry pipelines (Eng + Observability)
End-to-end QA with synthetic traffic harness and real customer pilot
Run pilot with two internal teams and one external beta customer, collect feedback

comments: 2026-01-18 — Kickoff: PMs, Eng leads, and Stats met. Agreed DSL should be YAML-first with a JSON-schema for validation. Action: Eng to draft runner API. (owner: Liam)

2026-01-22 — Decision: MVP statistical approach will use sequential frequentist checks with an alpha-spending schedule. Research to draft default schedules and recommended per-metric thresholds. (owner: Priya Nair)

2026-01-30 — Design review: Console templates mockups uploaded: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/EXP/Experiment+Templates. Design feedback: expose a 'safe mode' toggle that reduces exposure granularity to 0.1% steps for high-risk customers. (owner: Maria Gomez)

2026-02-03 — Eng update: Prototype Runner wired to Smart Routing in a staging cluster. Basic exposure caps enforced; still missing audit log entries. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runner/pull/412 (WIP)

2026-02-08 — Security: RBAC spec reviewed. Need a dedicated permission 'experiments.manage' and audit retention policy (90 days). Security review flagged data residency requirement for EU customers; add to acceptance criteria. (owner: Tom Harris)

2026-02-10 — PM update: Scope locked for MVP. Plan to schedule pilot with Search team in Cycle 2026-W10. Next steps: finalize DSL schema, schedule research integration for metric checks, build Console templates.
risks: Incorrect statistical defaults could lead to premature rollbacks or false sense of safety
Exposure controller bugs could route more traffic than intended (mitigation: deterministic cohort assignment + chaos tests)
Audit/compliance gaps for Private deployments requiring extra retention/air-gap handling
Operational complexity: adding another control-plane service increases SRE burden
notes: Consider a 'simulation mode' that runs the experiment offline against historical request logs to surface expected quality deltas before live exposure
Long-term: expand DSL to express hierarchical experiments (parent/child) and support multi-armed bandits with regret budgets
We should surface a conservative "safety score" computed from latency, error-rate, and quality regressions to help non-statisticians interpret results
Pilot success criteria: two pilot teams complete a 2-week canary with <1% regret and <24h mean time to rollback in triggered events
